第 85 章 To Code or Not to Code写代码还是不写代码

Ben Edmunds / 本·埃德蒙兹

— 第 231 页 —

If you've been an engineering manager for more than a few minutes, you've likely received the advice, "Stop coding!" You're a manager now, the value you bring to your team isn't in the code you produce. Or maybe you've received the exact opposite advice, "Always be coding!" You're a manager now, you don't want to lose your technical chops. Neither of these work well in my experience. Let me begin by explaining my own journey.

如果你做工程经理超过几分钟，你很可能收到过建议：「别写代码了！」你现在是经理了，你给团队带来的价值不在你生产的代码里。或者你收到完全相反的建议：「永远在写代码！」你现在是经理了，你不想失去技术功底。根据我的经验，这两个都不好。让我先解释我自己的历程。

Early in my management career I subscribed to the idea that you should continue coding. I was as active as ever, shipping as often as I did before, and trying to keep the same personal measures of success. This led to me working nonstop. I was attempting to fulfill my management duties during the day, then code all night. This caused alternating resentments. Either I would resent managing because it was interfering with coding, or I would resent coding because I had something I needed to handle on the management side. This was a horrible disservice to my team and to myself. I was a burned-out engineer and a horrible manager.

在管理生涯早期，我认同你应该继续写代码的想法。我和以前一样活跃，像以前一样频繁发布，试图保持同样的个人成功衡量标准。这导致我不停工作。我白天试图履行管理职责，然后整晚写代码。这造成交替的怨恨。要么我怨恨管理因为它干扰写代码，要么我怨恨写代码因为我在管理那边有事要处理。这对我的团队和自己都是可怕的伤害。我是一个倦怠的工程师和一个可怕的经理。

From here I swung to the other side. I attempted to stop coding. When I was coding, I saw it as a failure. It was a sign of my inability to delegate or plan well. This led to a constant state of frustration in myself and even more pressure on my team. I also started to see the effects of losing my technical edge and became removed from the constraints my team was working within. Finally, I settled into a workable balance between these two extremes. I hope my experience can help you find balance, as well. Here's what works for me, in priority order:

从这里我摆到另一边。我试图停止写代码。当我写代码时，我把它看作失败。那是我不能很好授权或计划的标志。这导致我自己持续的挫败状态和对团队更大的压力。我也开始看到失去技术优势的影响，脱离了团队工作的约束。最终，我在两个极端之间找到了可行的平衡。希望我的经验也能帮你找到平衡。以下是对我有效的，按优先级：

Management. This includes one-on-ones, planning, interfacing with other teams, and being available to your team.

管理。这包括一对一、计划、和其他团队对接、以及对团队有空。

Code reviews. This keeps me in the loop on what we're shipping.

代码评审。这让我在我们发布什么的圈子里。

— 第 232 页 —

Architecting. Performed with other engineers, I'm a sounding board and provide guidance.

架构设计。和其他工程师一起做，我是共鸣板并提供指导。

Fixing bugs. This is the majority of my coding now. I no longer have large blocks of focused time but often have 30- to 60-minute blocks. It's a great way to stay up to date on the day-to-day issues that your team is facing. It keeps you in touch with your codebases and it helps take some pressure off your team.

修 bug。这是我现在写代码的大部分。我不再有大段专注时间，但经常有 30 到 60 分钟的块。这是让你跟上团队日常面临问题的好方式。它让你和代码库保持联系，帮团队减轻压力。

Internal tools and automation. I try to identify tools that streamline internal processes or things that can be automated to save time. Often working it at a slow pace, as I get time. It might take me weeks to finish but that's ok as long as it's not urgent.

内部工具和自动化。我试图识别简化内部流程或可以自动化节省时间的东西。经常在有时间时慢慢做。可能花我几周完成，但只要不紧急就没关系。

My priorities might not work for you as is; you'll need to define your own. Here's how I recommend starting to explore this. First, being a manager is your top priority. Not empowering your team to be the best they can be is causing more damage than you not writing as much code. A team of people will always be more productive than you'll ever be. With that in mind, look at what responsibilities you have as a manager to determine what technical work fits within those constraints. It might be architecture, it might be writing documentation or requirements, it could be small features or fixing bugs. There could also be some subset of these things. The important part is being realistic with yourself on what you can do and how you can do those things while still putting your team's needs first.

我的优先级可能不直接适合你；你需要定义自己的。以下是我建议怎么开始探索。首先，做经理是你的最高优先级。不赋能团队做到最好比你不写那么多代码造成的损害更大。一个团队的人永远比你一个人多产。记住这一点，看你作为经理有什么责任，确定什么技术工作适合这些约束内。可能是架构，可能是写文档或需求，可能是小功能或修 bug。也可能是这些的某个子集。重要的部分是对自己现实地看你能做什么、你能怎么做这些事，同时仍然把团队需求放在第一位。

Next, redefine what success looks like for yourself. As managers, we don't get the constant dopamine hit of closing tickets and shipping code like we did as engineers. That's ok. Don't try to continue to feed your self-worth with those metrics. Write down a list of goals for your average week that includes both management and technical items. That might include things like one-on-ones, team meetings, or scheduling; along with planning the architecture for the next big feature and preforming code reviews.

接下来，重新定义对你来说成功是什么样。作为经理，我们不像工程师那样有关闭工单和发布代码的持续多巴胺刺激。没关系。不要试图继续用那些指标喂你的自我价值。写下你平均一周的目标清单，包括管理和技术项。可能包括一对一、团队会议或排程；以及下一个大功能的架构计划和做代码评审。

— 第 233 页 —

Finally, set your expectations and communicate them to your team and elsewhere. Ensure that everyone knows where your priorities are and why. This prevents miscommunication over why you aren't handling things others might expect from you. Write these priorities down in a clear way that you can reference.

最后，设定期望并沟通给团队和其他地方。确保每个人知道你的优先级在哪里和为什么。这防止关于你为什么不处理别人可能期望的事情的误解。把这些优先级以你可以参考的清晰方式写下来。

Most of all, understand that day-to-day tasks aren't set in stone. As a manager you need to be fluid and move to the issues that have the highest priority in the moment. Each day will be different from the last. Some days are for doing, some days are for talking and thinking, and some days are for fighting fires.

最重要的是，理解日常任务不是一成不变的。作为经理你需要流动，移到当下最高优先级的问题。每天都和前一天不同。有些天是做事的，有些天是谈话和思考的，有些天是救火的。
